result:
I've written `review-verdict.json` with a **reject** verdict.

Summary: the round-3 hardening genuinely closes the three bugs it claims to (config-file/env-var cgroup override, missing `+` strip, single-refspec checking), and the underlying dual-signal design plus PATH-wrapper mechanism is sound with real tests against the actual shipped snippet. But both wrappers detect the dangerous subcommand only at a fixed argument position — `git`'s check is `$1 == "push"` and `gh`'s is `$1/$2 == "pr"/"merge"` — so ordinary, common invocations with a global flag first (`git -C <dir> push origin master`, `gh --repo owner/repo pr merge 123 --merge`) skip detection entirely and reach the real binary unblocked. That's undisclosed and is the same recurring bug class (fixed-position argument parsing) the last three rounds each found and fixed elsewhere — it just wasn't caught here. No `.github/workflows/**` files are touched.
